acc-u4-l1: The bank statement shows interest received of ₦1,200 that is not in the cash book. What should be done?
Add ₦1,200 to the cash book balance
Deduct ₦1,200 from the cash book balance
Add ₦1,200 to the bank statement balance
Ignore it
The bank has credited interest; the cash book must be updated by adding it.
The bank already knows. Who needs to update their records?
A standing order for insurance of ₦3,000 was paid by the bank but not entered in the cash book. What should be done?
Deduct ₦3,000 from the cash book balance
Add ₦3,000 to the cash book balance
Deduct ₦3,000 from the bank statement balance
Add ₦3,000 to the bank statement
Money has left the account, so the cash book balance must be reduced.
Did money come in or go out?
A customer paid ₦8,000 directly into the business bank account (a credit transfer). It is not yet in the cash book. What should be done?
Add ₦8,000 to the cash book balance
Deduct ₦8,000 from the cash book balance
Deduct ₦8,000 from the bank statement balance
Ignore it until next month
Money has come into the bank, so the cash book must be increased.
The bank received money. Update the cash book.
The cash book shows ₦40,000. Bank charges of ₦500 have not been entered. What is the updated cash book balance?
Bank charges reduce the balance.
Why does a business prepare a bank reconciliation statement?
To explain the differences between the cash book and the bank statement
To calculate profit
To pay creditors
To value stock
It checks and explains why the two balances differ, and helps find errors or fraud.
Two records of the same account don't agree. Why?
The cash book shows ₦25,000. A credit transfer of ₦4,000 and bank charges of ₦1,000 are not recorded. What is the updated cash book balance?
Add money in, subtract money out.
Which of these items requires a correction in the CASH BOOK rather than the bank statement?
Bank charges
Unpresented cheques
Uncredited lodgements
An error made by the bank
Bank charges are known to the bank but not yet to the business, so the cash book must be updated.
Which item does the business not yet know about?
How are bank charges entered in the cash book?
On the credit side of the bank column
On the debit side of the bank column
In the discount column
In the cash column
Bank charges are money going out of the bank account, so they are credited.
Payments out are on which side?
A dividend of ₦5,000 is received directly by the bank. How is it entered in the cash book?
On the debit side of the bank column
On the credit side of the bank column
It is not entered
On the credit side of the cash column
Money received into the bank is debited in the bank column.
Money in goes on the debit side.
acc-u4-l2: An 'uncredited lodgement' is:
Money paid into the bank and recorded in the cash book, but not yet on the bank statement
A cheque the business issued that has not been presented
A charge made by the bank
A dishonoured cheque
It is a deposit the bank has not yet credited, a timing difference.
Lodgement means a deposit.
The bank statement shows ₦40,000. There is an uncredited lodgement of ₦6,000. What is the adjusted bank statement balance?
Add the lodgement to the statement: 40,000 + 6,000 = ₦46,000.
The bank will soon add this money.
Why is an uncredited lodgement NOT entered again in the cash book?
The cash book already includes it; only the bank statement is behind
It never happened
It is a bank error
It is always too small to record
The business recorded the deposit already; it's just a timing difference at the bank.
Who already knows about this deposit?
The bank statement shows ₦70,000 and there is an uncredited lodgement of ₦12,000. What is the adjusted bank statement balance?
Add lodgements to the statement balance.
An 'unpresented cheque' is:
A cheque issued and recorded in the cash book, but not yet paid by the bank
A deposit not yet credited
A cheque returned unpaid
A bank charge
The payee hasn't presented it yet, so the bank hasn't paid it.
Has the supplier banked it yet?
The bank statement shows ₦50,000; unpresented cheques are ₦9,000; uncredited lodgements are ₦4,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Subtract unpresented cheques, add uncredited lodgements.
The bank statement shows ₦20,000; uncredited lodgements ₦15,000; unpresented cheques ₦5,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Lodgements up, cheques down.
Which items are known as 'timing differences' in bank reconciliation?
Unpresented cheques and uncredited lodgements
Bank charges and interest
Dishonoured cheques and standing orders
Errors in the cash book
Both are already in the cash book and will clear at the bank soon; only the timing differs.
Which items just need time to clear?
Which of these adjusts the BANK STATEMENT balance, not the cash book?
An uncredited lodgement
Bank charges
A dishonoured cheque
Interest received by the bank
The cash book already has the lodgement; it is the statement that is behind.
Which item does the bank not yet know about?
acc-u4-l3: The bank statement shows ₦60,000. Unpresented cheques total ₦10,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
The bank will soon pay out these cheques.
The bank statement shows ₦35,000. Cheques of ₦4,000 and ₦6,000 have not been presented. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Total the unpresented cheques, then subtract.
Why are unpresented cheques deducted from the bank statement balance?
The bank has not paid them yet but will do so when they are presented
They are bank errors
They increase the bank balance
They were never written
The money will leave the account soon, so the statement balance is overstated for now.
What happens when the supplier finally banks the cheque?
The bank statement shows ₦18,000 and an unpresented cheque is ₦3,500. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Subtract.
A trader writes a cheque for ₦8,000 to a supplier and records it in the cash book. The supplier has not banked it yet. This is:
An unpresented cheque
An uncredited lodgement
A dishonoured cheque
A standing order
It has been issued but not yet presented for payment.
Has the bank seen it?
The cash book shows ₦45,000. The only difference is an unpresented cheque of ₦7,000. What does the bank statement show?
The bank hasn't paid the ₦7,000 out yet, so its balance is higher: 45,000 + 7,000 = ₦52,000.
The bank still has the money the cash book has already paid out.
The bank statement shows ₦90,000; unpresented cheques ₦12,000; uncredited lodgements ₦5,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Subtract cheques, add lodgements.
Reconciling from the cash book balance of ₦30,000 to the bank statement, with unpresented cheques of ₦4,000 as the only difference. What is the bank statement balance?
Starting from the cash book, add back the unpresented cheques: 30,000 + 4,000 = ₦34,000.
Working the other way, the sign flips.
The bank statement shows an overdraft of ₦10,000. There is an unpresented cheque of ₦5,000. What is the adjusted position?
An overdraft of ₦15,000
An overdraft of ₦5,000
A balance of ₦5,000 in hand
A balance of ₦15,000 in hand
When the cheque is paid, the overdraft will grow by ₦5,000 to ₦15,000.
Paying a cheque from an overdrawn account makes the overdraft bigger.
acc-u4-l4: A cheque the bank refuses to pay, usually because the drawer lacks funds
When a customer's cheque bounces, the bank refuses to honour it.
A customer's cheque for ₦12,000, already recorded and banked, is dishonoured. Which entry corrects the books?
The customer owes again (debit) and the bank balance falls (credit).
What is the effect of a dishonoured cheque on the cash book balance?
The receipt is reversed, so the bank balance goes down.
The cash book shows ₦50,000. A ₦6,000 customer cheque is returned dishonoured. What is the updated cash book balance?
After Bola's cheque is dishonoured, what is the position on Bola's account?
Reversing the payment restores Bola's debt.
The cash book shows ₦30,000. Not yet recorded: a dishonoured cheque ₦5,000, bank charges ₦500, interest received ₦1,500. What is the updated cash book balance?
Two items reduce it, one increases it.
The bank wrongly credited another customer's deposit of ₦2,000 to the business's account. How is this treated?
Deduct ₦2,000 from the bank statement balance
It is a bank error, so the statement is corrected, not the cash book.
A receipt of ₦7,500 was wrongly entered in the cash book as ₦5,700. What correction is needed?
7,500 - 5,700 = 1,800 was under-recorded, so add it to the cash book.
On the bank statement, a dishonoured cheque appears as:
A payment out (a debit on the statement)
The bank takes back the amount it credited, so it appears as money out.
The bank reverses its earlier credit.
acc-u4-l5: Bank statement ₦80,000; unpresented cheques ₦20,000; uncredited lodgements ₦15,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Subtract cheques, add lodgements.
Bank statement ₦120,000; unpresented cheques ₦35,000; uncredited lodgements ₦10,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Same method: minus cheques, plus lodgements.
Bank statement ₦45,000; unpresented cheques ₦5,000; uncredited lodgements ₦8,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Here the lodgements are bigger than the cheques.
The cash book shows ₦60,000. Bank charges ₦1,000 and a direct credit of ₦5,000 are not yet recorded. What is the updated cash book balance?
Update the cash book with what only the bank knew.
Bank statement ₦66,000; unpresented cheques ₦16,000; uncredited lodgement ₦4,000. What should the corrected cash book balance be?
Adjusted statement = 66,000 - 16,000 + 4,000 = 54,000. The corrected cash book must agree.
Both corrected balances must be equal.
After all adjustments in a bank reconciliation, what must be true?
The adjusted cash book and adjusted bank statement balances agree
The cash book balance is zero
The bank statement is always larger
Profit equals the bank balance
Reconciliation is complete when both adjusted balances are the same.
What does 'reconciled' mean?
Bank statement ₦200,000; unpresented cheques ₦50,000; uncredited lodgements ₦30,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Minus cheques, plus lodgements.
The cash book shows ₦40,000. Not yet recorded: a dishonoured cheque ₦3,000, bank charges ₦200, interest received ₦800. What is the updated cash book balance?
Two deductions, one addition.
Bank statement ₦55,000; unpresented cheques of ₦12,000 and ₦8,000; uncredited lodgement ₦9,000. What is the adjusted bank balance?
Add up the two cheques first.
acc-u5-l1: Where there is no partnership agreement, how are profits shared under the Partnership Act?
Without an agreement, partners share profits and losses equally.
What is the fair default when nothing is agreed?
Where there is no partnership agreement, is interest allowed on capital?
The Act allows no interest on capital unless the partners agree to it.
Interest on capital must be agreed.
A partner lends the firm money, and there is no agreement on interest. What rate of interest is the partner entitled to?
Under the Partnership Act, partners' loans earn 5% per annum.
Loans are treated differently from capital.
Ade (capital ₦500,000) and Bola (capital ₦100,000) have no partnership agreement. Net profit is ₦90,000. What is Bola's share?
With no agreement, profit is shared equally: 90,000/2 = ₦45,000, regardless of capital.
Does the size of capital matter without an agreement?
Where there is no partnership agreement, are partners entitled to salaries?
The Act gives no salaries to partners unless agreed.
Salaries must be agreed in advance.
Three partners have no agreement. Net profit is ₦120,000. How much does each receive?
A partner lends the firm ₦200,000 and there is no agreement on interest. How much interest is due for a year?
The written agreement that sets out the rules of a partnership is called:
The partnership deed sets out capital, profit sharing, salaries and interest.
Which of these is NOT usually found in a partnership agreement?
The names of the firm's customers
Agreements cover partners' rights and rewards, not customer lists.
Which item is not about the partners?
acc-u5-l2: Partners share profits 3:2. Residual profit is ₦50,000. What is the larger share?
Add the ratio parts: 3 + 2 = 5.
Partners share profits 2:1. Residual profit is ₦90,000. What is the smaller share?
Total parts = 3.
Partners share profits 5:3. Residual profit is ₦160,000. What is the larger share?
Total parts = 8.
Three partners share profits 1:1:2. Residual profit is ₦200,000. What does the third partner receive?
Total parts = 4. Third partner: 2/4 * 200,000 = ₦100,000.
Chidi and Emeka share profits 3:2. Residual profit is ₦100,000. What is Emeka's share?
Emeka has the 2 in 3:2.
Residual profit in a partnership is:
The profit left after partners' salaries and interest on capital
Gross profit
Profit before expenses
The total of drawings
Salaries and interest are taken out first; what remains is shared in the ratio.
What is left after the agreed payments?
Net profit ₦150,000; partners' salaries ₦30,000; interest on capital ₦20,000; profits shared equally. How much residual profit does each of the two partners get?
Find the residual first.
Net profit ₦120,000; interest on capital A ₦6,000 and B ₦4,000; ratio 3:2. What is A's share of the residual profit?
Take out both partners' interest first.
A partnership makes a loss of ₦30,000, shared 2:1. How much of the loss does the larger partner bear?
Losses are shared in the same ratio as profits.
acc-u5-l3: A partner brings in a car worth ₦800,000 as capital. Which entry is correct?
Debit Motor Vehicle, Credit Partner's Capital
Debit Partner's Capital, Credit Motor Vehicle
Debit Cash, Credit Capital
Debit Motor Vehicle, Credit Sales
The firm receives a vehicle (debit); the partner provides capital (credit).
What does the firm receive?
A partner takes ₦20,000 cash for personal use. Which entry is correct?
Debit Partner's Drawings, Credit Cash
Debit Cash, Credit Partner's Drawings
Debit Partner's Capital, Credit Sales
Debit Wages, Credit Cash
Drawings are debited; cash leaves the firm (credit).
Same as a sole trader's drawings.
Interest on a partner's capital is credited to:
The partner's current account
The trading account
The bank account
The partner's loan account
It is a reward to the partner, credited to the current account and debited to the appropriation account.
Where do partners' rewards collect?
A partner's salary is recorded as:
Debit Appropriation account, Credit Partner's Current account
Debit Profit and Loss, Credit Cash
Debit Partner's Current account, Credit Appropriation account
Debit Wages, Credit Bank
A partner's salary is a share of profit, not an expense, so it goes through the appropriation account.
Is a partner an employee?
Under the fixed capital method:
Capital accounts stay unchanged; profit shares and drawings go to current accounts
Profits are added straight to capital accounts
There are no capital accounts
Drawings are added to capital
Fixed capital keeps the capital account steady and uses current accounts for the year's items.
What stays 'fixed'?
Interest charged on a partner's drawings is recorded as:
Debit Partner's Current account, Credit Appropriation account
Debit Appropriation account, Credit Partner's Current account
Debit Cash, Credit Drawings
Debit Drawings, Credit Bank
Interest on drawings is a charge to the partner and adds to the profit to be shared.
The partner pays this, so his account is debited.
A new partner pays ₦100,000 by cheque into the firm as capital. Which entry is correct?
Debit Bank, Credit New Partner's Capital
Debit New Partner's Capital, Credit Bank
Debit Cash, Credit Sales
Debit Bank, Credit Goodwill
The bank receives money (debit); the partner provides capital (credit).
A cheque goes into the bank.
A partner lends the firm ₦200,000 by cheque. Which entry is correct?
Debit Bank, Credit Partner's Loan account
Debit Partner's Capital, Credit Bank
Debit Bank, Credit Partner's Capital
Debit Loan account, Credit Bank
A loan is kept separate from capital: debit Bank, credit the partner's loan account.
Is a loan the same as capital?
Where is interest on a partner's LOAN to the firm charged?
In the profit and loss account, as an expense
In the appropriation account
To the partner's drawings
To the partner's capital account
Loan interest is a business expense charged before profit is appropriated.
A loan is like borrowing from a bank.
acc-u5-l4: A partner's current account opens with a ₦10,000 credit. He gets salary ₦20,000, interest on capital ₦5,000, profit share ₦40,000, and draws ₦30,000. What is the closing balance?
A current account opens with a ₦5,000 DEBIT. The partner's profit share is ₦30,000 and drawings are ₦20,000. What is the closing balance?
A debit opening balance counts as a minus.
A credit balance on a partner's current account means:
The partner has left the firm
The firm has made a loss
Credits are amounts due to the partner that have not been drawn.
A current account opens at zero. The partner's profit share is ₦25,000, interest on drawings is ₦1,000 and drawings are ₦30,000. What is the closing balance?
Interest on drawings is a charge to the partner.
Which items are CREDITED to a partner's current account?
Salary, interest on capital and share of profit
These are rewards to the partner.
Which items are DEBITED to a partner's current account?
Drawings, interest on drawings and share of loss
These reduce what the firm owes the partner.
Opening credit ₦8,000; salary ₦12,000; interest on capital ₦3,000; profit share ₦27,000; drawings ₦35,000; interest on drawings ₦500. What is the closing balance?
Total the credits and the debits separately.
Opening debit ₦2,000; share of loss ₦6,000; salary ₦10,000; drawings ₦4,000. What is the closing balance?
A loss is a debit, like drawings.
Opening credit ₦15,000; interest on capital ₦5,000; profit share ₦20,000; drawings ₦25,000. What is the closing balance?
acc-u5-l5: Net profit ₦180,000. Salary for A ₦30,000. Interest on capital: A ₦10,000, B ₦10,000. Residual shared equally. What is A's total share?
Add A's salary, interest and residual share.
In the same partnership (profit ₦180,000; A's salary ₦30,000; interest ₦10,000 each; equal sharing), what is B's total share?
B gets interest 10,000 + residual 65,000 = ₦75,000.
B has no salary.
Net profit ₦100,000. Interest on capital ₦8,000 and ₦4,000. Interest on drawings ₦1,000 from each partner. Shared equally. What residual share does each partner get?
Interest on drawings is ADDED to the profit available.
What is the correct order in the appropriation account?
Net profit + interest on drawings - salaries - interest on capital = residual profit
Net profit - interest on drawings + salaries = residual
Gross profit - drawings = residual
Residual + salaries = net profit - drawings
Add interest on drawings, deduct partners' salaries and interest on capital, then share what is left.
Adjust first, then share.
Net profit ₦240,000. Salary for B ₦40,000. Interest on capital: A ₦20,000, B ₦20,000. Residual shared 3:1 (A:B). What is B's total share?
Find the residual, then B's quarter of it.
Net profit ₦60,000. Salaries: ₦30,000 for each of two partners. Interest on capital total ₦10,000. What is the residual profit or loss?
A residual loss of ₦10,000
A residual profit of ₦10,000
A residual profit of ₦50,000
Zero
60,000 - 60,000 - 10,000 = -10,000: a residual loss to be shared.
Appropriations can be bigger than the profit.
The partnership appropriation account shows:
How net profit is shared among the partners
The cost of goods sold
The firm's assets and liabilities
Cash received and paid
It distributes net profit as salaries, interest and shares of profit.
'Appropriate' means to set aside for someone.
Net profit ₦90,000. Interest on capital is 10% on capitals A ₦200,000 and B ₦100,000. Residual shared equally. What is A's total share?
10% of each capital first.
How is interest on partners' drawings treated in the appropriation account?
It is added to net profit before sharing
It is deducted from net profit
It is an expense in the profit and loss account
It is ignored
It is a charge paid by partners to the firm, so it increases the profit available to share.
Who pays this interest, and to whom?
acc-u6-l1: A club's accumulated fund is ₦200,000 at the start of the year and it makes a surplus of ₦30,000. What is the closing accumulated fund?
A surplus adds to the fund.
A club's accumulated fund is ₦150,000 at the start of the year and it makes a deficit of ₦20,000. What is the closing accumulated fund?
A deficit reduces the fund.
In a non-profit organisation, the accumulated fund is the equivalent of:
Capital in a business
Sales
Drawings
Liabilities
The accumulated fund is the members' interest, like a trader's capital.
What is the owner's stake called in a business?
A club has assets of ₦300,000 and liabilities of ₦40,000. What is its accumulated fund?
Accumulated fund = assets - liabilities = ₦260,000.
Same idea as capital = assets - liabilities.
In a club's income and expenditure account, a surplus means:
Income was greater than expenditure
Expenditure was greater than income
The club has no cash
The club made sales
A surplus is the non-profit word for a profit.
Surplus = something extra.
A non-profit organisation's income and expenditure account takes the place of a business's:
Profit and loss account
Balance sheet
Cash book
Bank statement
It shows income, expenses and the surplus or deficit for the year, like a P&L.
Which business statement shows profit?
A town union's accumulated fund rises from ₦90,000 to ₦110,000 during the year, with no other changes. What was the surplus?
The increase of ₦20,000 must come from the surplus.
The change in the fund = surplus or deficit.
At the start of the year, a club's assets are ₦120,000 and liabilities are ₦20,000. What is the opening accumulated fund?
Assets minus liabilities.
How is a deficit treated in the club's balance sheet?
It is deducted from the accumulated fund
It is added to the accumulated fund
It is shown as a current asset
It is added to subscriptions
A deficit reduces the members' fund.
A deficit is like a loss.
acc-u6-l2: A club starts the year with cash of ₦20,000. It receives ₦150,000 and pays out ₦130,000. What is the closing cash balance?
Opening + receipts - payments.
A receipts and payments account is:
A summary of the club's cash book
The same as an income and expenditure account
A list of members
A balance sheet
It summarises all cash and bank receipts and payments for the period.
Does it follow cash or accruals?
Opening cash ₦10,000; subscriptions received ₦80,000; donations ₦20,000; payments ₦95,000. What is the closing cash?
Add all receipts first.
Which items does a receipts and payments account include?
All cash received and paid, whether capital or revenue and whatever period it relates to
Only revenue items for the current year
Only items owed at the end of the year
Only non-cash items like depreciation
It is purely about cash moving, so all cash items go in.
Is it about cash or about the year's income?
A club starts with an overdraft of ₦5,000. It receives ₦60,000 and pays ₦50,000. What is the closing position?
A balance in hand of ₦5,000
An overdraft of ₦5,000
A balance of ₦15,000
An overdraft of ₦15,000
An overdraft is a negative opening balance.
What is the main difference between a receipts and payments account and an income and expenditure account?
Receipts and payments is on a cash basis; income and expenditure follows the accruals concept
They are the same
Income and expenditure only records cash
Receipts and payments shows depreciation
Income and expenditure adjusts for amounts owing and prepaid; receipts and payments only shows cash.
Which one includes depreciation and accruals?
Opening cash ₦30,000; receipts ₦100,000; payments ₦140,000. What is the closing position?
An overdraft of ₦10,000
A balance of ₦10,000
A balance of ₦70,000
An overdraft of ₦40,000
Payments are bigger than the money available.
A club pays cash for a new bus. Where does this payment appear?
In the receipts and payments account, but not in the income and expenditure account
In the income and expenditure account only
In neither account
In the income and expenditure account as an expense
Cash was paid, so it is in receipts and payments; the bus is an asset, so it is not an I&E expense.
Is the bus an expense or an asset?
Opening cash ₦25,000; levies ₦60,000; bazaar ₦40,000; hall hire paid ₦50,000; refreshments paid ₦30,000. What is the closing cash?
Total receipts, total payments, then work it out.
acc-u6-l3: A club paid rent of ₦50,000 during the year and ₦5,000 is still owing at the end. Nothing was owing at the start. What is the rent expense for the year?
Expense = paid + owing at end = 50,000 + 5,000 = ₦55,000.
Include what was used but not yet paid.
A club paid ₦60,000 rent this year, including ₦10,000 owing from last year. Nothing is owing at the end. What is this year's rent expense?
Remove last year's part: 60,000 - 10,000 = ₦50,000.
Some of the payment belongs to last year.
A club paid ₦30,000 insurance, of which ₦3,000 is prepaid for next year. What is this year's insurance expense?
Prepaid amounts belong to next year: 30,000 - 3,000 = ₦27,000.
Remove the part for next year.
A club paid electricity of ₦24,000. ₦2,000 was owing at the start and ₦4,000 is owing at the end. What is the electricity expense?
Minus opening owing, plus closing owing.
The accruals concept states that expenses should be recorded:
In the period they are incurred, not when they are paid
Only when cash is paid
Only at the end of the business's life
When the bill is received
Expenses are matched to the period they relate to.
Match costs to the time they were used.
A club paid ₦40,000 for a service. ₦4,000 was prepaid at the start of the year and ₦3,000 is owing at the end. What is the expense?
40,000 + 4,000 (prepaid used this year) + 3,000 (owing) = ₦47,000.
An opening prepayment is used up this year.
How is rent owing at the year end shown in the balance sheet?
As a current liability
As a current asset
As part of the accumulated fund
As income
Rent owing is money the club owes, so it is a liability.
Does the club owe it or own it?
How is insurance prepaid at the year end shown in the balance sheet?
As a current asset
As a current liability
As an expense
As capital
A prepayment is a benefit still to come, so it is an asset.
The club has paid for something it hasn't used yet.
A club paid wages of ₦100,000. ₦8,000 was owing at the start and ₦5,000 is owing at the end. What is the wages expense?
Take out last year's part, add this year's unpaid part.
acc-u6-l4: A club received ₦90,000 subscriptions, including ₦5,000 for last year. Members still owe ₦4,000 for this year. What is this year's subscription income?
Remove last year's money, add this year's unpaid amount.
A club received ₦50,000 subscriptions, including ₦6,000 paid in advance for next year. What is this year's subscription income?
Next year's part is removed: 50,000 - 6,000 = ₦44,000.
Money for next year is not this year's income.
How are subscriptions in arrears (owed by members) at the year end shown in the balance sheet?
As a current asset
As a current liability
As an expense
They are not shown
Members owe the club, so it is an asset, like debtors.
Who owes whom?
How are subscriptions received in advance at the year end shown in the balance sheet?
As a current liability
As a current asset
As income
As part of the accumulated fund
The club owes members a year of membership, so it is a liability.
The club has been paid for something it hasn't given yet.
A club received ₦70,000: ₦3,000 was for the previous year and ₦2,000 for next year. Members owe ₦4,000 for this year. What is this year's subscription income?
Keep only this year's subscriptions.
